key_insight: Across ABO2 oxides, delafossite and related layered variants can be as thermodynamically competitive as infinite-layer phases, especially for Ni, Pd, and Pt systems.
engineering_relevance: For synthesis and device design, the results identify which cation combinations and hole-doping strategies are most likely to stabilize target infinite-layer oxides relevant to correlated-electron and superconducting applications.
method: High-throughput first-principles calculations across the AB O2 phase space
Phase-diagram comparison of infinite-layer, perovskite-like, delafossite, and ordered rock-salt (111) structures
Electronic-structure analysis of Fermi-surface character and cation ordering
evidence_signal: The study evaluates relative thermodynamic stability and electronic structure trends from comprehensive computational screening over the periodic table, highlighting La-Ni as the best infinite-layer candidate and showing Ca/Sr/Ba doping improves stability.
watch_item: Thermodynamic favorability does not guarantee experimentally accessible synthesis, especially for bulk substrate-free infinite-layer oxides and phases constrained by kinetics or cation ordering.
paper_title: Delafossites as an unexpected competing phase to infinite-layer oxides
